minutes.headline: Gas station special permit not decided; hearing continued to Nov 12 after applicant dropped 24-hour operation.
minutes.summary: The board heard opposition from Stone Farm residents, neighbors and their attorney, then the applicant's attorney, engineer and traffic consultant on a revised plan with the car wash removed, fewer pumps and a smaller building. Members raised concerns about property values, lighting, noise, driveway width and the pylon sign. The applicant agreed to change hours to 5 a.m.–11 p.m., and the hearing was continued so he can return with revised plans.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals did not decide the gas station special permit and continued the hearing to November 12 at 7 p.m.
The applicant asked to withdraw the 24-hour operation and proposed hours of 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.; the minutes record the vote outcome on this as not audible.
The applicant will return with revised plans covering the sign, lighting and buffers.
The revised plan removes the car wash, reduces the pumps and shrinks the building.
Stone Farm residents and neighbors spoke against the project; one speaker supported the owners' right to commercial use.

why_it_matters: The permit decision is still open, so residents near Mass Ave and Riley Road, including Stone Farm, can still weigh in on hours, lighting, noise, traffic and the sign before the board rules.
watch_next: Continued hearing on November 12 at 7 p.m., where revised plans for the sign, lighting and buffers are expected.
